newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Sept 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Sept 12.

text.p: - Christian vigilantes in Mindanao said they will fight to keep their weapons in defiance of President Ramos' order for their disbandment. The small Christian militia group was formed recently in Mindanao to oppose the government's peace deal with Moslem rebels. (PHILIPPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- Businessmen in Mindanao are on a "shopping spree" in Metro Manila for high-powered rifles in anticipation of a renewed escalation of the Christian-Moslem conflict in the South, according to a ranking Camp Crame official. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- Chairman Nur Misuari of the Moro National Liberation Front and former regional speaker Guimid P. Matalam were proclaimed on Wednesday as winning candidates for governor and vice-governor, respectively, of the Autonomous Region in Moslem Mindanao. (MANILA BULLETIN)
- Environment department officials on Wednesday reimposed a ban on shellfish after two persons were reportedly poisoned after eating mussels from Manila Bay. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- A 70-year old Filipino-Chinese businessman was released by kidnappers on Tuesday night after his family paid a ransom of two million pesos, sources in the Filipino-Chinese community said. (THE PHILIPPINE STAR)

- Kidnapping incidents nationwide increased by 46 percent from January to September this year compared to the same period last year, National Police Director General Ricaredo Sarmiento said. The police had recorded 108 kidnappings during that period compared to 74 incidents last year, he said. (THE MANILA TIMES)

- The row over the Club John Hay bidding has reached a climax as the Bases Conversion Development Authority declared the winner, Manuela Land & Houses Corp, in default. The state-owned firm will award the contract to the second highest bidder, Penta Capital Investment Corp and Fil-Estate Land Inc. (THE BUSINESS DAILY)
- Mitsui Corp of Japan is planning to put up a multi-billion peso integrated food processing plant at the Bataan Export Processing Zone. (THE BUSINESS DAILY)
